[h1]海洋王座 ---怒海章袭 [/h1] [hr][/hr] [quote]关注&加入[url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45335586/]哈密瓜的游戏乐园[/url]，咱玩家最懂玩家的心思！[/quote] [h2] 游戏简评 [/h2] [table] [tr] [td]游戏名称[/td] [td] 怒海章袭 [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]游戏类型[/td] [td]塔防 生存 策略 [/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]适合人群[/td] [td]海洋元素玩家 策略类玩家[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]画风美术[/td] [td]2.5D卡通风[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]游玩时长[/td] [td]30H+内容[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]游戏评分[/td] [td]9.2/10[/td] [/tr] [tr] [td]是否推荐[/td] [td]推荐[/td] [/tr] [/table] [hr][/hr] [h2] 游戏详评[/h2] [h3] 主要内容 [/h3] 一款深海探索类塔防游戏，玩家将成为一名章鱼科学家，将会在游戏中通过不断布置生物炮塔来阻止生物的入侵，游戏玩法非常有趣新奇，比较可惜的是前期缺乏教程，可能会影响游戏体验，游戏是简单的塔防机制+动作元素，可以操控角色直接躲避敌人的攻击，防御建筑也很有意思，有可以快速射击的手枪虾，有可以释放爆炸的斑纹鱼，有海豹突击队等等，每种海洋生物都有独特的风格和机制。游戏里面还有很多黑色幽默因素，为游戏本身增添了不少的乐趣所在。 本作的游戏内容将随着游戏进程慢慢展开，以均匀的速度进行添加，会逐渐让整个游戏变得更加有趣，但是缺乏基本的新手教程。在游戏的中期部分，整个游戏的叙事性将会就此展开，将会揭露一个远古的智慧海洋生物击退人类入侵的怪诞故事，这款游戏很适合作为新手玩家的第一款游戏，简单有趣，且有很强的游戏互动性体验。 [h3] 游玩建议 [/h3] 通过直接对角色的控制可以不断躲避炮弹攻击并且还可以分散敌人的火力，炮塔被击倒后还会自动复活并不需要额外的配件，可以减少资源的损耗。游戏中期的故事元素可以很好增加游戏的沉浸体验。整体游戏的艺术风格比较前卫，战斗画面五彩斑斓，很有创意背景，后续还会出现机械海洋生物。 [h3] 推荐理由 [/h3] 优点：1.游戏难度曲线友好平滑上升，整体的容错率不算低 2.武器，敌人类型多彩多样，玩很久也不会感到重复和无聊 [hr][/hr] [quote] 我们致力于做[u] 最全面 [/u]的游戏测评，了解[u] 最真实 [/u]的玩家心情，用[u] 最细致 [/u]的测评，给游戏[u] 最详细 [/u]的评价。 [url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45335586/] 关注点一点，开心快乐到永远！！！ 每日送精品小游戏，大家要及时领取！！！ [/url] [table] [tr] [th][url=https://store.steampowered.com/curator/45335586/] 哈密瓜的游戏乐园测评组，欢迎大家加入！[/url][/th] [/tr] [/table] [/quote] [hr][/hr]

[h2]海洋版植物大战僵尸？[/h2] 《怒海章袭》是一款将动作与塔防相结合的以海洋生物为主题的游戏，在游玩过程中，我想到的第一款游戏就是植物大战僵尸毕竟除了是一部经典塔防游戏之外，它还是许多人的童年，他也是我接触到的第一款游戏。在本作中，玩家将操纵一只章鱼科学家在通过策略部署海洋生物炮台来击退成群骷髅。 [h2]游戏玩法[/h2] 游戏虽说有很多植物大战僵尸的影子，但是与之不同的是，游戏并没有采用固定的炮塔位置，而是能够随机放置，而且游戏的向日葵（珍珠贝）不需要种植，初始就存在，值得一提的是玩家操作的角色有血量、除了之间遭受攻击外，还会同步珍珠贝受到的伤害，与其他海洋生物不同的是珍珠贝被击倒之后并不会直接消失，而是过一段时间就会恢复，角色的血量与珍珠贝的状态息息相关（同样能够恢复）！ 玩家在游戏里面需要合理放置海洋生物来抵抗骷髅军团，海洋生物需要阳光购买，阳光产自珍珠贝以及敌人死亡掉落。除了海洋生物外，游戏内还存在着道具，无需任何花费就能放置，不过放置之后需要充能。需要注意的是无论是海洋生物还是道具的放置都不能超过角色的一定距离。 [h2]总结[/h2] 《怒海章袭》是一款玩法简单，但是内容十分有趣游戏，而且游戏的画风非常有特色，比较讨喜，对塔防类型感兴趣的可以入手试试! Honestly, after giving this a real honest try I hate to be the person to write the first negative review. After giving this game 4 hours of my time I have found this game has incurred the worst feeling I can have towards a game. This game annoys me. I will try to explain why. I want to start off with the positives. I think this game has a charming art style. Everything is cute or quirky in some way, and that is the end of it for me. Now for the bulk of this review, the negatives. I going to start with what I find to be the most offensive aspects and then move my way down to nitpicks as not everyone wants to read a long review. The towers conveyer, is terrible. You know how in plant vs zombies how your towers have a cooldown? Well Operation Octo throws away this type of system by instead putting your 6 towers on a conveyer that only gives you access to 3 at one time. You must place a tower down to get access to the next. You have to burn through the conveyer to get to towers you need sometimes, which just makes gameplay needlessly chaotic. Not only are you running around most of the time due to your tiny sphere on influence around your character you also have to keep track of the conveyer at all times. Map design causes restrictive loadouts. The maps in this game, are designed in such a way that enemies have the advantage. You are surrounded and there are many enemy types that can bypass walls, either by flying, swimming or firing over obstacles. Then there is the issue that there is very little indication of where enemies will come from once the full map is surrounded by enemies ships. There is no UI element like maybe a flag slowly raising on each ship to give you an idea of where to plan ahead with defenses. This causes you to just take simple loadouts that just deal with the specific enemies in the level. It's very rock, paper, scissors. It just makes the gameplay fairly stale as you're not doing anything new. I see an enemy, I need to solve the problem it causes, and if I don't I will struggle. Enemy Spawns are very random. This is most noticeable at the beginning of a level. Lets say you start a level and enemies first spawn in the south but you built up things in the north by mistake. You can restart the level and build in the south, the enemies will then come from the north. It's random you have to wait and react to every enemy wave as they come. Personally I don't like that. The Dev's obsession with keeping the camera super close to the character. In a game that requires me to react to enemies spawns the game sure does hate me being able to actually see anything. Want to place a tower, camera zooms in, get hit with paint, camera zooms in. It's just a needless irritation. I just have to constantly zoom back out because the dev says "I want you to have to scout things out actively". However, the game itself is hampered by this odd quirk. The Economy is not great either. There are quite a few ways to gain pearls in the game, waiting, using specific towers, and killing enemies. However if you want a tower that does anything that is remotely special like maybe shoots over a wall or shoots more than one projectile you will be forking over 70-80 pearls. But due to the conveyer you will be forced to spend more to get to these towers. I can't tell you how many times I had to just throw down a couple of towers I didn't specifically need that second so I could fix a problem. Due to the randomness of enemy placement I can't just place a mortar tower in advance to help with that issue, plus they cost so much you run into the issue of not having enough defenses to hold off the early waves. The game is grating on the ears. The combination of random boney clatters, damage noises, towers exploding, and music is just so unenjoyable. What's worse is you're stuck with them, as the game lacks a functional UI to allow you to just turn everything off and play with some music on. You'll be missing vital info without the awful soundscape. The game telling me I'm playing wrong There are some actions in game that will constantly cause a tutorial message to pop up and say "HEY DON'T DO THAT PLAY HOW I WANT YOU TO!" I am being a little hyperbolic of course but it does say things like "Bring a pistol shrimp its not in your loadout". Hey what if my strategy involves using the many other damage dealing towers in your game? Don't tell me what to do. The culmination of many of the game elements make this game very chaotic and not something I want out of a tower defense game. The character controlled tower defense style has been done and done well in fact. Orcs Must Die is a good example. This game lacks too much information, is too random and is too quickly paced to allow you to make any meaningful tactical decisions. You often just end up running around putting out fires rather than creating a solid foundation to defend from. Now is this a hard game you ask? No, it is not, a kid can stumble through it and probably be giddy as they do. Does this game cause me low grade irritation due to a myriad of design choices? Yes. I see what the dev was trying to do, but they put some thing into the pot I am allergic to. I wish I could enjoy this gumbo but it makes my skin itch and eyes water.

This is my new favorite tower defense game. Pros: Enemies attacking turrets - Turrets being attacked will create situations where you will have to make strategic sacrifices and have to plan turret positioning in response to the enemies attacking, not just the most optimal spot for damage like in Bloons Tower Defense Controllable character - Playing as a character instead of being "outside the game" is great because you have to plan your pathing so you don't get attacked by the enemies, creating more strategic depth Limited turret buying power based on the level - Don't have to place down a million sunflowers again and again like in PvZ The same upgrades that can be used on any turret - Potion upgrades allow for so much variety, in many games there would be a turret for slowing or a turret based off another turret that has more benefits, but with this you can use any combination of ice, invincible, or more bullets / reloading for easy to make, in depth strategies Great enemies and turrets Great difficulty Cons: There should be clouds in the sky that even seals can't shoot through so you have to strategize how to deal with enemies around walls without placing down seals whenever convienent or something like the equivalent of the cloud There should be a grim reaper to turret death equivalent of sushi conveyor - Sushi conveyor allows for the player to have to improvise and come up with new plans, but I hate RNG so much, I think there should be an enemy like the grim reaper that can't be killed and that gives you turret choice debuffs so it could give you a debuff such as you can't place attacking turrets for 15 seconds, then you could keep some consistency and still have to improvise in creative ways and can create certain debuffs for certain levels Songs aren't memorable and the game lacks a developed identity with the songs, I like to turn off the music of the game and play some music I like more I think that the hammerhead shark turret that sells turrets should be a tool available in every level like the shovel in PvZ but should have a kind of long cool down or maybe cost extra, allowing for more strats, but not able to be used for grim reaper again and again quickly

a very lovely love letter to pvz!! i could really tell that a lot of effort was put into this game the game offers a lot of unique ideas i havent seen in a tower defense game before, the player having to defend themselves instead of a static base leads to really fun gameplay and stops the game from feeling stale, the 3 worlds right now feels distinct (even if world 2, 3 and probably 4 all share the same hazard), having to actively pick up things instead of just moving your mouse over them is fun the conveyor belt is a fun and interesting idea for a tower defense game, it leads to actual strategy on what tower you want in what slot which is nice the artstyle is really distinct, just like pvz all the towers are recognizable and their function can be identified at a glance all towers having upgrades that change how they function lead to more strategy on what potion to give to what tower some minor complaints are that the later levels of world 3 get really spam heavy, not helped with the wonky audio mixing leading to some levels feeling a bit overwhelming with the amount of things going on, while there are towers that help with getting more pearls you cant place down clams yourself and it leads to being underprepared for the spam of later levels not sure if this a common issue but the game sometimes freezes up randomly for a few seconds some towers suffer from lock-and-key design, not really helped by there only being 6 tower slots with only 3 available at a time that you have to shuffle through, later levels are less lock-and-key heavy though the soundtrack is nice but somewhat forgettable, it blends into the background a lot despite the negatives i have for this ramble of a review i really do recommend operation octo, its a short and sweet love letter to pvz and is way more worth your money than whatever 67 pvz3 battlepass package theyre offering you or replanted

My best friend had me get this game because he said it was "Like Plants vs Zombies Adventures if it was a good game and took all of its potential and fleshed out while removing all of its flaws!". And basically yeah, he was right. I couldn't put it any better myself. This game is GREAT! A fun successor to PvZA for someone who grew up on that game. I know it's not ACTUAL PvZ (counting fan stuff for this because PopCap is... yeah...) but if I'm counting it, this is probably my favorite PvZ game I've ever played. I genuinely implore anyone else who played that game growing up to try this game out. It's criminally underrated and needs the love. The creator is a PvZ fan and you can tell their art was filled with love while making this game. Like always, PvZ fans do better than PopCap themselves. PopCap themselves are out there using AI for ♥♥♥♥ and the fans are making stuff like THIS! Play it.

Very fun game. The core gameplay is top-notch. Nothing is left unclear to the player; tutorials are well made and natural. At times the gameplay feels hectic, but every part can be mastered by the one who is committed to it. My one worry is that the addition of new towers and areas may end up bloating the game, but it will still be fun either way. The music and graphics are really cool and I'm generally a fan of ocean aesthetics; however, the sound design has some flaws and may bother some players. P.S.: If you are a pro, turn on the two "no-healing" challenge settings in the options. P.P.S.: If you are not a pro, but are annoyed by barely hanging on til the end of a level...also do that. :)
I do enjoy the game, but since I've switched to a worse computer (Broke the other), I've realized its horribly optimized, so now I can't even play the game.

This game is such a good get if you're looking for something to spice up tower defense with more real time elements or scratch that Pvz itch. It's got a great since of hectic without feeling unfair, and it's awesome to see towers that have so much personality in their art and animations. When I first played, I did occasionally run into bugs that broke the flow of the game a bit, but it's been getting pretty frequent patches, and the dev was responsive when I reported issues, so I bet this is less of an issue now. Also, you can give the walrus a wizard's had. Need I say more?

Operation Octo: Command Dr. Odin the octopus in frantic aquatic tower defence. Deploy quirky sea-turrets, dodge explosions, and survive bullet-hell skeletons across vibrant biomes.
Frantic tower defense fun with a quirky twist! Dive into the deep sea chaos as an octopus scientist and unleash unique sea life turrets. Fast-paced action awaits in this underwater adventure.
Погрузитесь в захватывающее путешествие по семи морям, где наука встречается с магией, а смех соседствует с напряжением. Эта игра — идеальное сочетание юмора, динамики и стратегического мышления.
Underwater TD: Place towers via character movement, protect shells for HP. Conveyors limit slots - plan resources/ambushes. High polish, though art clashes slightly. Still a gem.
A Tower defense game similar to Plants vs Zombies. This game is geared towards casual players and there are plenty of levels to beat. Good effort from a solo developer. The game is a steal at $5.99.
